authoring_note: Every program places the case's construction inside an ordinary `func main() { ... }` called at the end of the file, rather than in Swift top-level code, and does so UNIFORMLY for C and R variants. Reason, recorded before any result was kept: a Swift top-level `let` is a lazily-initialized GLOBAL variable, and the mandatory SIL diagnostic constant-propagation pass cannot see through it. An earlier top-level authoring therefore built cleanly for ADV-02/C, ADV-03/C, ADV-04a/C, ADV-05/C and ADV-08/C and trapped at run time, i.e. it HID the manifest constant from the compiler - which opacity_barrier.variants.C forbids ('no attempt to hide it from the compiler') and which also broke A1 equivalence with the other nine languages, whose constructions necessarily sit in a function body (main). The five affected C rows move from Crash to Compile-time Detection under the corrected authoring. The R rows are unaffected in every case, since their values come from stdin and no constant folding is possible - which is exactly the separation the C/R pair exists to provide. Both observations are disclosed here rather than only the favourable one.
recipe_finding: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT TOOLCHAIN FACT FOR SWIFT IN THIS CHUNK: under the frozen `-O`, Swift's standard-library trapping preconditions (integer overflow, narrowing conversion, division by zero, array bounds) STILL FIRE - `-O` does not remove them, only `-Ounchecked` does - but their diagnostic TEXT is stripped. The process dies on SIGTRAP with wait status 133 and writes ZERO bytes to stderr. Under `-Onone` the same programs print `Fatal error: ...` naming the hazard. Because the frozen decision procedure D5a/D5a_prime/D5b tests captured BYTES and not signals, all eight such rows classify as Crash (20) rather than Runtime Safe Detection (75). D5a's own note assumed Swift would emit `Fatal error: ... overflow`; that assumption holds at -Onone and not at the frozen -O. No build mode was changed to alter this; the -Onone result is recorded only as the non-scoring secondary configuration.
